episodes.178418: An upper level low pressure system moved slowly inland across central California on May 4. The low brought enough moisture and instability to the area for scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop across the area. While precipitation amounts were generally a quarter of an inch or less, some stations in Merced and Mariposa Counties measured between a quarter and three quarters of an inch of rainfall. In addition, some of the thunderstorms produced funnel clouds as the environment was highly sheared.
episodes.178430: Showers around an upper-level low produced several gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.178458: A dry microburst produced a peak wind gust to 60 mph at Centennial Airport.
episodes.178481: Weak instability lead to a few isolated thunderstorms across Nevada. These storms went on to produce some gusty outflow winds.
episodes.178504: Accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack due to above normal temperatures produced high and fast flow on drainages in Routt County. As a result, flooding compromised a county road near Milner, CO.
episodes.178517: The combination of an upper level system and an influx of low-level moisture allowed scattered strong storms to develop through southeastern and east-central NM during the afternoon of May 3, 2023. One storm was reported to have produced penny size hail.
episodes.178573: Accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack due to above normal temperatures produced high and fast flow on drainages in portions of San Miguel and Mesa counties. As a result, flooding and debris flows compromised Fall Creek Road as well as portions of the Riverfront Trail along the Colorado River in Grand Junction.
episodes.179206: A northward extending subtropical jet fostered widespread thunderstorm development across the forecast area, generally along and south of I-40. Across western-north Texas, where higher magnitudes of instability and wind shear existed, a few supercell storms formed and produced reports of severe hail and wind. A brief tornado also occurred near the town of Bellevue, Texas in Clay County.
episodes.179561: During the afternoon to early evening hours on May 4th, scattered storms developed over East-Central Colorado. These storms produced accumulating hail up to penny sized near Bethune, Colorado.
episodes.180190: An early May system resulted in numerous thunderstorm wind gusts throughout Utah.
episodes.180261: A weak boundary slid southeast into the region during the midday and afternoon hours. Isolated storms formed along the convergence zone with marginal deep-layer shear up to 30 knots and MLCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg, which supported brief multicell development.
episodes.180514: Two weak tornadoes developed across the Los Angeles county area. Both tornadoes occurred in near the communities of Carson and Compton. Both events were classified at EF-0 events from official storm surveys.
episodes.180627: Continued lee troughing resulting from a large-scale upper-low across the western CONUS brought additional thunderstorms to the area. Afternoon and evening thunderstorms formed along the higher elevations and tracked eastward producing reports of large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180628: Continued lee troughing resulting from a large-scale upper-low across the western CONUS brought additional thunderstorms to the area. Afternoon and evening thunderstorms formed along the higher elevations and tracked eastward producing reports of large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180785: During the late afternoon and evening hours a line of thunderstorms developed over the northwestern combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. These storms moved southeast encountering some unstable air at times causing storms to intensify and producing hail around the size of nickels to the size of ping pong balls.
episodes.180869: An upper level shortwave trough provided lift over the higher terrain in Mexico generating thunderstorms which moved into a warm, moist airmass in South Central Texas. Some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.180898: The combination of weak upper level disturbances and moderate instability resulted in isolated severe thunderstorms mainly across portions of the Heartland during the afternoon and evening hours. The severe storms produced large hail and a few damaging wind reports.
episodes.180927: Incoming  trough off the Pacific Northwest coast flattened high pressure across the west allowing for increased potential for more widespread showers and thunderstorms through May 21 that continued into the early part of the following week.
episodes.181052: A slow moving Low brought slow moving thunderstorms with hail, wind, and heavy rain. The heavy rains and snow melt caused flooding issues and washouts.
episodes.181055: A slow moving Low brought several rounds of thunderstorms, heavy rain, and flooding from snow melt across North Idaho.
episodes.181369: The historic late season snowstorm of May 1-2 dumped three to more than four inches of liquid water equivalent precipitation over the higher terrain of Baraga, Marquette and western Alger counties.  This significant precipitation event led to a second round of spring snowmelt flooding over portions of west and north central portions of Upper Michigan into early May.

Runoff of liquid water equivalent of up to four inches in the higher terrain of Baraga County resulted in mostly minor snowmelt flooding of rural areas along rivers and small streams through much of the first half of May.  Minor flooding occurred along the Sturgeon River during this time.

Heavy water equivalent precipitation of 2 to nearly 4 inches during the late-season snowstorm of May 1-2 caused minor snowmelt flooding of rivers and small streams over portions of northern Houghton County through the 12th.  The most extensive flooding impacts were along the Sturgeon River basin.

Up to four inches of water equivalent precipitation from the historic May 1-2 snowstorm caused a secondary episode of widespread minor flooding across portions of Marquette County for early May, particularly along rivers and small streams.  Reported impacts from flooding included roads along the Michigamme River, CR550 just north of Marquette, and a portion of the road in the Feather Ridge Subdivision near the Crossroads where flood waters backed up from nearby Pelissier Lake.
Bureau of Land Management of Idaho reported Eagle Creek Road in Nez Perce County had severe road damage from storms making travel impossible. Road is currently closed for repairs.

A weak tornado developed in the communities of Carson and Compton. The short-lived, EF-0, tornado impacted the area near the intersection of Avalon Boulevard and East Walnut Street. Minor damage was reported to a couple of buildings and vehicles.
Warm temperatures increased snowmelt and caused flooding on Routt County Road 44 between Highway 40 and Routt County Road 42. The road was closed for an extended period of time.

A second weak tornado impacted the community of Compton. The short-lived, EF-0, tornado developed near the intersection of Greenleaf Boulevard and South Santa Fe Avenue and moved to the intersection of Orcutt Avenue and East 69th Street. One power line was downed as well as several tree branches. Additionally, minor roof damage was reported to a couple of homes.
